text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Illinois are currently targeted by fake traffic and toll violation text scams, spoofed bank calls, and home improvement contractor fraud.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake traffic and toll violation text scams, spoofed bank calls, and home improvement contractor fraud

list.snippet: Fake Traffic & Toll Texts: Scammers send text messages claiming your driving privileges will be suspended for 30 days or that you owe unpaid traffic/toll fines . They include a phishing link to steal personal data. (Note: The Illinois Secretary of State only texts for DMV appointment reminders, never for fines or penalties).

Spoofed Bank Phone Calls: Fraudsters use spoofed caller IDs to make calls look like they are coming from real local institutions like Central Bank Illinois or "Fraud Departments" to trick you into sharing sensitive banking details .

Home Improvement & Construction Fraud: Year-after-year, home repair and construction scams rank among the most frequent complaints to the Illinois Attorney General’s office. Contractors take a large down payment and then fail to show up or finish the job.

Impersonation Scams: Scammers pose as state government agencies, law enforcement, the IRS, or the DMV, or direct people to fraudulent registration websites like illinoiscarreg.com instead of official portals .
Do not click links: Never tap on links in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding tolls, traffic tickets, or license renewals.

Verify independently: If you get a suspicious call or text from a bank or government agency, hang up and call the official phone number listed on their verified website. Use official portals like ILSOS.gov for vehicle and driver services.
Report scams: You can log and report fraudulent activity through the BBB Scam Tracker or file a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov .

text_blocks.snippet: If you received a specific text, call, or email you are unsure about, share what the message or caller claimed and I can help you check if it matches a known scam pattern.
